headline: Saimemory, a SoftBank unit, has signed a deal with Shinko Electric to help bring its ZAM memory toward production.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an announced memorandum of understanding; the technology is still in R&D.
importance_line: What changed: a Japanese memory project has added a packaging partner on its way to production, which matters to AI chip makers looking for alternatives to HBM; ZAM is still in R&D, no production date is given, and the view that it is an alternative to HBM is the author's reading.
summary: Semiecosystem reports that Saimemory, a Tokyo-based unit of SoftBank, has signed a memorandum of understanding with Shinko Electric, a Japanese maker of chip packaging parts, to develop and commercialise its Z-Angle Memory (ZAM), a next-generation memory technology. ZAM is still in research and development and appears to be an alternative to high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked memory that AI chips rely on and that is in short supply; Saimemory also signed an earlier deal with Intel this year to commercialise it.
